title: Owning complex enterprise cybersecurity opportunities
scope: Full-cycle enterprise selling: new business, expansion and account strategy.
collaboration: Technical evaluators and commercial stakeholders across enterprise buying groups.
decision: Connect the technical evaluation to each stakeholder's business problem and the decision the buying group needs to make.
context: An enterprise security opportunity needs more than a successful technical evaluation. Buyers also need a business case and alignment across the people involved in the decision.
contribution: At Forcepoint, I owned new-logo and expansion opportunities across the Mid-Atlantic and Southeast and closed enterprise web-security deals. At Rapid7, I led strategic enterprise opportunities, including threat intelligence.
execution: I used technical discovery to shape the account plan and connected the evaluation to the business problem in commercial conversations. My responsibility was to carry the opportunity across those conversations, keeping technical validity, business value and stakeholder alignment connected.
evidence: My public career timeline records full-cycle enterprise selling at Forcepoint and Rapid7, including closed web-security business and strategic threat-intelligence opportunities.
takeaway: The seller's job is to help the buying group reach an informed decision. Technical proof, business value and stakeholder alignment need to move together.
reviewer: Pending Kristen Aing review of enterprise sales, GTM ownership and leadership copy
